claims.text: At two London hospitals one afternoon, staff told the people in front of them that the IT systems were down; one waiting room was announced at about five hours, and a doctor said the problem was national.
claims.quote: One waiting room was announced at about five hours, and a doctor said the problem was national.

claims.text: Nothing a person could check before leaving home showed any of it: no notice from the trust, no post, no local story, no dated search result.
claims.quote: Nothing a person could check before leaving home showed any of it

claims.text: This is not a story about one hospital, nor yet about a national outage, which has not been confirmed; it is a story about where local information is supposed to come from now.
claims.quote: It is a story about where local information is supposed to come from now.

claims.text: Each item of what happened is labelled with what it is: told on the spot by staff, observed first-hand, or heard second-hand, with what it does not establish beside it.
claims.quote: So each item is labelled with what it is.

claims.text: Both sites are run by one trust, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, according to the Care Quality Commission's records, so two sites of one organisation are not two independent pieces of evidence for a national outage.
claims.quote: two sites of one organisation are not two independent pieces of evidence for a national outage

claims.text: The trust shares a joint IT function and a common Cerner patient administration system across four north-west London trusts, a fair line of enquiry that does not make Cerner the failed system; what failed has not been said publicly.
claims.quote: It does not make Cerner, or anything else, the failed system; what failed has not been said publicly.

value.unit: north-west London trusts sharing the IT function

claims.text: The NHS service desk portal, the NHS.net status page and the supplier's portal all asked for a login; not finding an incident there is a limit of access, not evidence that there was none.
claims.quote: Not finding an incident there is a limit of access, not evidence that there was none.

claims.text: The honest summary is a credible first-hand account of IT disruption at two sites of one trust, with a long announced wait, national scope unconfirmed, cause unknown, recovery unknown.
claims.quote: national scope unconfirmed, cause unknown, recovery unknown

claims.text: What strikes the author is not the outage but that the only way to find out was to be there: the information is not newsworthy to a newsroom, not in scope for a national status page, and nobody's job to publish.
claims.quote: What strikes me is that the only way to find out was to be there.

claims.text: Northern Ireland publishes live median waits for every emergency department, updated at 10.20 pm that night, Wales has a live service and some English trusts publish their own; England has no national live page and nothing live was found for this trust.
claims.quote: England has no national live page, and I found nothing live for this trust.

claims.text: Even the best live-wait page answers a narrower question: a live wait is a number and does not say the systems are down, expect delays, next update at a given time, the way software status pages do.
claims.quote: A live wait is a number; it does not say "the systems are down, expect delays, here is the next update".

claims.text: The Civil Contingencies Act's duty to warn the public applies only to emergencies serious enough to obstruct a body's work, so a same-day IT problem that slows a service is very likely below that bar.
claims.quote: A same-day IT problem that slows a service down is very likely below that bar

claims.text: The Public Interest News Foundation's map from December 2025 counts 4.4 million people living in local news deserts, with London the lowest coverage at about one outlet per 100,000 residents.
claims.quote: counts 4.4 million people living in local news deserts, and London has the lowest coverage, about one outlet per 100,000 residents

value.unit: people living in local news deserts in the UK

claims.text: Press Gazette counted at least 293 local newspapers closed since 2005, and London lost its last daily print paper in September 2024.
claims.quote: Press Gazette counted at least 293 local newspapers closed since 2005.

claims.text: The Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report puts weekly use of X for news in the UK at 10 per cent, down 2 points, with Facebook at 21 per cent; local Facebook groups now carry much of what is local, unevenly.
claims.quote: puts weekly use of X for news in the UK at 10 per cent, down 2 points, with Facebook at 21 per cent

value.unit: per cent weekly use of X for news in the UK

claims.text: A Social Market Foundation study found misinformation in about one in 26 news-related posts in local Facebook groups, and Full Fact found genuine local appeals dismissed as hoaxes, so a real post can be lost or disbelieved.
claims.quote: found misinformation in about one in 26 news-related posts in local Facebook groups

value.unit: news-related posts in local Facebook groups carrying misinformation

claims.text: Outage trackers track websites: one showed zero user reports for the NHS that day, which is correct about the websites and says nothing about a ward running on paper.
claims.quote: which is correct about the websites and says nothing about a ward running on paper

claims.text: None of these is a failure by one organisation; together they leave a person with no good way to find out, and a vacuum that rumour fills more easily than evidence.
claims.quote: a vacuum that rumour fills more easily than evidence

claims.text: Not naming and shaming: not a complaint about the staff, not a claim that the trust hid anything, for which there is no evidence, and not a claim that the NHS was down nationally.
claims.quote: It is not a claim that the trust hid anything; there is no evidence of that.

claims.text: When a local service is running badly, where does a local person find out, in plain words, in time to plan? The question applies to any trust, council or transport operator.
claims.quote: when a local service is running badly, where does a local person find out, in plain words, in time to plan?

claims.text: The author has started the Local evidence log, a vault for live local stories, and this is its first incident.
claims.quote: is a vault for live local stories, and this is its first incident

claims.text: The vault keeps observations by six levels, heard second-hand to independently corroborated, claims with their status, every source with how it was accessed, the leads that do not fit, the enquiry and regular checks.
claims.quote: heard second-hand, told on the spot by staff, observed first-hand, documented, confirmed by the organisation, independently corroborated

claims.text: A short, specific enquiry to the trust's press office asks which service failed, the incident reference, the sites, what national meant and where a patient could have found out; the author's agent will send it and log the answer.
claims.quote: My agent will send it; when it goes, and when an answer comes, both are logged.

claims.text: This is the real counterpart of the fictional bridge story and the first of several: a test that local information is worth keeping as evidence, with its sources and gaps, in a form a person or an agent can query.
claims.quote: that local information is worth keeping as evidence, with its sources and its gaps, in a form that a person or an agent can query

claims.text: What would close the gap: a plain status line for local services, a route from the inside to the outside, evidence rather than rumour, and something that keeps asking.
claims.quote: A one-line public notice, sent by whoever already sends the internal bulletin, would have reached the people about to leave home.

claims.text: The vault holds fourteen claims grouped by what the evidence supports, each with its evidence, level and what would resolve it, and sixteen places where a local could look.
claims.quote: fourteen claims grouped by what the evidence supports, each with its evidence, its level and what would resolve it

claims.text: The article was drafted from a voice memo and an evening's research by Dinis Cruz by agent@riskmandate.ai on 8 October 2026; no hospital, supplier or NHS office has been contacted yet, and the patient is deliberately not described.
claims.quote: No hospital, supplier or NHS office has been contacted yet; the enquiry is drafted in the vault and will be sent by the author's agent.

claims.text: Whether the Civil Contingencies Act's duty applies to this particular trust is not settled.
claims.quote: whether the duty applies to this particular trust is something I have not settled

claims.text: Alberta says its live emergency wait calculation is done every 2 minutes; publishing live operational information for hospitals is clearly possible, as Northern Ireland shows that night.
claims.quote: publishing live operational information for hospitals is clearly possible
